## Problem statement

The system has recurring crashes that are not being reported or reviewed:

- /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash - a 616 MB crash dump from Aug 17 (node process)
- 10+ chrome-headless int3 traps in the kernel log across Aug 18-20
- /var/crash/kdump_lock and kexec_cmd exist but no kdump crash dumps are captured (kernel crash handling not generating reports)

Crash dumps are accumulating (616 MB is significant) without review or reporting, meaning recurring crash patterns go unnoticed until they cause a system outage (as happened on 2026-08-20).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verify whoopsie/apport crash reporting is functional (systemctl status whoopsie, apport status) and report generation is enabled
- [ ] Review the existing /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash dump and record what it reveals (what crashed, why) in a comment on this work item; decide whether to keep or purge it (616 MB)
- [ ] Confirm whether kernel crash reporting (kdump/kexec) is configured to capture the next kernel panic; if not, either configure it or document why it is intentionally disabled
- [ ] Ensure crash dumps are rotated/aged so they cannot fill the disk (e.g. whoopsie retention settings or a cleanup job)
- [ ] Document the crash-reporting setup and retention policy in a comment on this work item or docs

## Key files / commands

- /var/crash/, whoopsie/apport config (/etc/default/apport, /etc/whoopsie)
- `apport-cli` / `whoopsie` status, `du -sh /var/crash`
- Discovered from: RCA of system hang 2026-08-20 (session analysis; no parent work item)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-04T06:28Z Plan: pre-check returned decision=skip (Extra Small effort, Low risk). Ran all six automated review stages — all passed. ACs fully traceable and testable. Marked plan_complete. No child work items created (sufficiently scoped as single chore).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MR24H2VK004PAQ7** – 1a: Error Classification & Settings (tests) (completed)
- **WL-0MSALMGTH002YXN7** – Foreign-item detection and dry-run report (completed)
- **WL-0MSF1656I008R145** – Fix: worklist pane CWD resolution when invoked from a Work Items plugin pane (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `CLI.md` — matched: automatic, bin, cannot, cause, check (+70 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: analysis, automated, automatic, bin, changelog (+63 more)

data.comment:
Crash dump review — /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash (WL-0MT1KJNMV0018SWP AC2)

File: /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash — 490251823 bytes (468 MB), mtime 2026-08-29 12:35:38, owner rgardler:whoopsie (0640)

Metadata:
- ProblemType: Crash, Architecture: amd64, DistroRelease: Ubuntu 26.04
- Package: nodejs 22.22.1+dfsg+cs22.19.15-1ubuntu1, ExecutablePath: /usr/bin/node
- ProcCmdline: node (vitest 6), ProcCwd: /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine
- Signal: 6 (SIGABRT), Uname: Linux 7.0.0-30-generic x86_64, CoreDump: base64 (full process memory)
- ProcStatus: VmPeak 5.3 GB, VmRSS 4.3 GB, VmData 4.3 GB, Threads 7, CoreDumping 1
- Stacktrace/StacktraceTop/StacktraceAddressSignature: absent — apport did not run gdb retrace, only ProcMaps + raw CoreDump present

Interpretation:
- SIGABRT in a vitest worker (vitest 6) at ~4.3 GiB RSS. Typical abort from V8 CHECK/assertion or --max-old-space-size OOM, consistent with browser-mode vitest holding a large Chromium renderer plus JS heap. See docs/dev/chrome-headless-concurrency-memory-profile-investigation.md.
- No actionable stacktrace; the 468 MB is almost entirely base64-encoded core. Textual metadata is <1 MB.
- Unrelated to the kernel int3 traps / NVIDIA Xid 119 GPU timeouts mentioned in the work item (those are headless-shell NVRM API-mismatch / GPU RPC timeouts; most recent kernel trap was electron[3853159] trap int3 on 2026-09-02, not Node).

Decision: purge (or let apport cron prune by ~2026-09-06; /etc/cron.daily/apport purges >7d).
RCA value is low without a stacktrace; cost is high (96% of /var/crash). Keep optional header excerpt for provenance: head -c 65536 /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash > /tmp/node-crash-2026-08-29.header.txt, then rm /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash. Details and runbook in docs/dev/crash-reporting.md §5.

Verification snapshot (2026-09-05):
- apport: enabled=1, core_pattern piped to apport, service enabled — OK
- whoopsie: binary 0.2.82ubuntu present, but whoopsie.path is disabled (inactive dead) — WARN — needs sudo systemctl enable --now whoopsie.path
- kdump: USE_KDUMP=1, kdump-tools.service enabled and crash kernel loaded (/var/lib/kdump/vmlinuz -> /boot/vmlinuz-7.0.0-30-generic, kexec_cmd present) — OK
- retention: /etc/cron.daily/apport present (prunes >7d; zero-byte files immediately) — OK
- disk: 468 MB total, largest 468 MB — within 1024/500 thresholds — OK (cron will prune the single large file ~2026-09-06)

Producer actions:
- Enable whoopsie.path: sudo systemctl enable --now whoopsie.path && systemctl status whoopsie.path
- Purge old dump when convenient: rm /var/crash/_usr_bin_node.1000.crash (or let cron do it)
- Verify: scripts/crash-reporting-check.sh and scripts/crash-reporting-check.sh --json (docs/dev/crash-reporting.md §6)
